assessments.reasoning: Calling the synchronous generator function produces its iterator. Advancing the iterator starts execution. At a reached yield, suspension preserves local bindings, the execution position, evaluation stack, and exception-handling state for resumption.

challenge.method: Distinguish creating an iterator and never advancing it from advancing it until a yield. Check the adjacent async def case.
challenge.results: Creation alone need not reach any yield. State retention applies when execution actually suspends there. The reference explicitly directs asynchronous generators to a separate description.

limitations: The passage applies to synchronous generator functions. Asynchronous generators have separately documented methods.
This tests an ordinary synchronous generator reaching yield. It does not prescribe behavior when an earlier statement exits or raises.
Runtime observations use the installed CPython 3.13.5 Windows build. The documentation scope comes from the pinned 3.13.0 source.
